name: typescript-helper
description: Helps with TypeScript tasks where a type check did not run, ran on a different axis than expected, or reported nothing that was being read for — reaching for `any` where `unknown` is inert outbound and would keep the call chain checked, indexing into an array with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` off so `arr[0]` is typed present whether or not it is, turning `strictNullChecks` off so every nullability annotation becomes decorative, reading control-flow narrowing as a constraint on assignment when assignability is checked against the declared type, treating an `in` check as an exclusive partition when optional properties survive in both branches, running under `module: esnext` so the compiler never checks the output for Node.js compatibility, hitting Node's "double default" where the same import works transpiled and is not a function natively, trusting a compiler option whose default is derived from a flag the config never mentions, and using `!` or `as` where no runtime check is performed at all.
